A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RBC watermarking work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are readable, and relocated or renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v3 reports original watermark detection, perturbation robustness, perplexity, hyperparameter, and SimCSE experiments in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v5 reports original experiments, including retained watermark evaluations and new PRC comparisons, calibration, decoder analyses, instruction-tuned evaluation, QA quality measurements, and detection timings.

M1.justification: The RBC generation and detection algorithms, sliding-window construction, binary sampling channel, and alternative statistical tests are retained. v5 newly explains the practical belief-propagation decoder; the PDFs do not establish that it replaced a previously used decoder. Exact decoding is added as an experimental comparison.

E1.justification: v5 adds long-form question answering on 200 ELI5 examples from WaterBench in Appendix C.5, substantially extending coverage beyond the existing open-ended generation tasks. The original prompts, English–Russian translation scenario, and other perturbation types are retained.

E2.justification: PRC, previously discussed as related work, becomes an evaluated comparator in the main detection and robustness experiments and the retained OPT and Mistral experiments. This adds a closely related ECC-based comparison throughout the evaluation. EXP-Edit, KGW, Token Specific, and one-to-one RBC remain.

E3.justification: The main detection threshold changes from 10^-4 to 10^-6; EXP-Edit retains its 10^-2 exception. New instruction-tuned evaluations use 10^-2. v5 also introduces unwatermarked calibration controls, decoder configurations, a 200-example ROUGE QA protocol, and detection timing procedures, while dropping the SimCSE assessment.

E4.justification: v5 adds empirical false-positive calibration in C.1, sensitivity to decoder bit-error probabilities and comparison with exact decoding in C.4, and runtime analysis in C.6. The existing code-size and perturbation studies remain, while the SimCSE quality analysis is removed. The localized watermark example is retained.

E5.justification: The retained experiments continue to specify 100 generations per prompt and report standard errors. The BC, GLRT, and PGLRT procedures are unchanged. New experiments extend the reported evidence without introducing a new uncertainty estimator, seed policy, confidence-interval method, or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Results are extensively revised and expanded. In Table 1, LDPC's 30-token geometric mean p-value changes from 6.0e-6 to 5.5e-6, while detection changes from 58.5% to 34.4% under different thresholds, not a comparable-setting decline. PRC, calibration, decoder, instruction-tuned, QA, and timing results are added; SimCSE results are removed.

T1.justification: The ECC and entropy definitions, entropy bounds, mismatch theorem, exact-block-decoding theorem, and Appendix D proofs retain their mathematical content. Theorem 4.3's equality is displayed separately in v5, but the statement is equivalent.

C1.justification: The experimental summary narrows its blanket assertion from 'consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baseline methods' to 'consistently performs well.' The abstract, numbered contributions, and Section 6 otherwise retain the principal robustness, detectability, and generation-quality claims.

C2.justification: v5 explicitly excludes adaptive watermark-aware attacks, discusses reduced detectability for instruction-tuned models and strong perturbations, and explains practical versus exact decoding and decoding overhead. These refine applicability and implementation interpretations; the existing limitation concerning whole-generation distortion-freeness remains.

D1.justification: v5 adds a reproduction-code link and identifies belief propagation under a binary symmetric channel, clarifying the already-listed p=0.35 parameter. Conversely, it removes v3's compute disclosure specifying two Nvidia 3090 GPUs and 24 GPU hours. These are documentation changes, not evidence of a changed implementation.

R1.justification: v5 adds WaterBench and ELI5 references, removes the SimCSE reference, and expands the discussion of Qu et al. with a single-bit equivalence claim concerning KGW. The substantial PRC positioning already existed in v3. Piet et al.'s publication update refers to the same work.

P1.justification: There is localized copyediting, terminology and cross-reference cleanup, updated affiliations, added acknowledgements, and appendix subsection reorganization. The main six-section narrative and most methodological and theoretical prose remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v5 adds calibration and instruction-tuned quality figures plus instruction-tuned detection and runtime tables, while removing the SimCSE violin plot. Existing displays gain PRC curves and rows, median columns, and decoder-ablation rows. Table 2 moves from the appendix into the main text; the qualitative figure is retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v5 substantially strengthens empirical support by directly evaluating PRC, supplying instruction-tuned results already claimed in v3's abstract, and testing decoder choices and detection speed. Calibration and clearer applicability limits further improve assessability. The gains outweigh the removed SimCSE and compute disclosures, although the 1,000-text calibration study cannot establish false-positive control at 10^-6.
